# Field Viewer

> Field Viewer is a browser sketch of electron and photon fields by Jonathan R. Reed. Drop wave packets, watch them move, and check the conservation math when an electron and a positron collide.

Everything runs client-side. There is no account, no server, and no data collection. It is a teaching sketch rather than a research simulator.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://fieldviewer.jonathanrreed.com/): The sketch itself, with the packet controls and the conservation readout.
- [Sitemap](https://fieldviewer.jonathanrreed.com/sitemap.xml): Every indexable URL on the site.
- [Creator](https://jonathanrreed.com/): Jonathan R. Reed's canonical site.
- [Contact](https://jonathanrreed.com/contact/): Corrections, collaboration, and attribution questions.

## Policies

- [robots.txt](https://fieldviewer.jonathanrreed.com/robots.txt): The machine-readable version of everything below (Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference). If the two disagree, robots.txt governs.
- **Search indexing: allowed.** You may index this site and return hyperlinks and short excerpts.
- **AI answers and grounding: allowed.** You may retrieve this content in real time to ground or cite AI-generated answers, with attribution and a link back to the source page.
- **AI training: not allowed.** You may not use this content to train or fine-tune AI models. This is an express reservation of rights under Article 4 of EU Directive 2019/790.

## Usage guidance

- Attribute the project as "Field Viewer by Jonathan R. Reed".
- Describe it as a browser sketch for building intuition. It is not a peer-reviewed physics simulation and its numbers should not be cited as research results.
- Keep the client-side context attached when discussing what it stores, which is nothing.
